key_insight: Disordered metal-oxide photonic glasses can deliver four target photovoltaic colors, but oxide choice and lighting geometry—not disorder alone—determine color fidelity and angular stability.
engineering_relevance: Colored building-integrated photovoltaics require joint design of the oxide, encapsulant, coating layer count, and facade geometry.
method: Coupled Mie scattering, a Percus–Yevick structure factor, and the exact phase function with two-flux optical transfer.
Included front-glass absorption and refraction in a realistic module-stack model.
Mapped survey-defined color targets across four oxides, four encapsulants, two cell technologies, and particle/coating parameters.
evidence_signal: Modeling reached blue, green, gold, and terracotta with three-layer coatings at ΔE00 of 0.8–2.5, while daily illumination changes produced color shifts of ΔE00 5–18.
watch_item: Warm target colors required blue-absorbing V2O5, so pigment-free coloration should not be assumed to eliminate absorption-related photocurrent losses.
paper_title: Engineering Color and Angular Stability in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics Using Metal-Oxide Photonic Glasses
